title: Statewide agent-based model for management of chronic wasting disease in white-tailed deer: PAOvCWD
author: Wehr, Rosenberry, et al.

steps.title: Generate landscape rasters
steps.instruction: Create ASCII raster files of percent forest cover for each Pennsylvania wildlife management unit (WMU) in a format required by NetLogo.

substeps.instruction: Download the public WMU shapefile (23 polygons) and dissolve internal boundaries to produce a single‑polygon outline of Pennsylvania; optionally dissolve a user‑provided study‑area shapefile.
Import the 2019 National Land Cover Database (NLCD) raster at 30‑m resolution covering the entire Pennsylvania shapefile.

Reclassify NLCD cells: assign value 1 (forested) to shrub, woody wetland, and all forest classes; assign value 0 (unforested) to open water, herbaceous wetland, all developed classes, barren, grassland, pasture, and crops.
Aggregate the 30‑m cells by a factor of 53.6 to produce ~1 mile² (2.59 km²) cells; compute each cell's value as the mean of the underlying 1/0 values, yielding percent forest cover (0–1).
Split the statewide raster into 22 current WMU rasters (WMU 2H merged into 2G, WMU 2H removed) by cropping to each WMU polygon and masking values outside the polygon within an iterative loop.
Export each WMU raster as an ASCII file with “no data” values set to 0.
Re‑import each ASCII file, change the no‑data value from 0 to –9999, and re‑export to the NetLogo model folder so that NetLogo interprets the files correctly.

Resulting ASCII files have cells inside WMU boundaries with values between 0 and 1, cells outside with 0, and a global no‑data value of –9999; NetLogo will treat cells with percent forest cover < 0.05 as unsuitable deer habitat.

steps.title: Curate deer demographic CSV
steps.instruction: Produce a comma‑separated values (CSV) file containing demographic parameters for white‑tailed deer for each WMU and a statewide average.

substeps.instruction: Obtain 12‑year (2012–2023) averages from the Pennsylvania sex‑age‑kill model supplied by the Pennsylvania Game Commission.

Calculate for each WMU the following columns: Unit, Population_Density (deer per mile²), Sex_Ratio (females per 100 males), Prop_A_Females (proportion ≥ 30 months), Prop_Y_Females (≈ 18 months), Prop_A_Males (≥ 30 months), Prop_Y_Males (≈ 18 months), Adult_Male_Harvest (rate), Yearling_Male_Harvest (rate), Antlerless_Harvest_Rates (rate for females of all ages and males < 12 months).
Do not calculate proportions for 6‑month‑old deer because the PAOvPOP model handles those implicitly.
Compute a statewide average by taking the mean of each column across the 22 WMUs.
Save the resulting dataframe as a CSV file; this file will be imported into NetLogo in Step 3.

steps.title: Initialize deer population with PAOvPOP
steps.instruction: Run the PAOvPOP NetLogo model via the nlrx R package to generate post‑harvest deer population CSVs for each WMU.

substeps.instruction: Install NetLogo and Java (Oracle) and copy the NetLogo csv and palette extensions into the same folder as the PAOvPOP model (or copy the model into the extensions folder).
In R, load the nlrx package and define internal file paths to the Java executable, NetLogo installation, and PAOvPOP model file.

Create an nlrx experiment matrix specifying: runtime = 25 months (two years of natural fluctuation plus one month to trigger the export action), region = WMU identifier, recommended_parameter_values = statewide average harvest mortality, and output = post‑harvest population CSV required for Step 4.
Initialize a separate nlrx simulation for each of the 22 WMUs and run them, exporting the resulting CSV files.

Use the future package to parallelise the simulations: set split = number of cores (e.g., 11 cores for 22 WMUs), ensuring the number of simulations is divisible by the core count; on an i7 processor with 64 GB RAM this required ≈ 3 hours of wall‑time.

steps.title: Simulate CWD transmission with PAOvCWD
steps.instruction: Execute the PAOvCWD NetLogo model via nlrx to simulate chronic wasting disease spread and management responses over ten years.

substeps.instruction: Copy the NetLogo csv and palette extensions into the folder containing the PAOvCWD model (or place the model in the extensions folder).
Choose an implementation method:

a. Personal‑computer workflow: an R markdown file that defines file paths, builds an nlrx model matrix, and uses the future package to assign computational cores (typical run time 4–8 h on an i7 with 64 GB RAM).
b. High‑performance‑computing workflow: an R script plus a plain‑text parameter file submitted to the Roar Collab HPC cluster via the clustermq package; each core receives 8 GB RAM.
For either method, construct an nlrx experiment matrix with the following settings:
• runtime = 121 months (10 years + 1 month to trigger result export).
• cwd_region = WMU identifier.
• statewide_average = TRUE (use statewide harvest rates for model stability).
• analysis = TRUE (required for nlrx; FALSE would run a visual NetLogo simulation).
• infection_seed = 3 (initial infected deer; values < 3 can cause early disease extinction).

• Six equal percentages (user‑defined) specifying the proportion of each demographic class that is tested for CWD among hunter‑harvested deer; these percentages are varied to affect time‑to‑detection.
• response = one of: "None", "Targeted_Culling", "Add_DMAP", "Alter_Antlerless_Harvest", "Alter_Antlered_Harvest", or "All".
If a response other than "None" is chosen, also define the following parameters (user‑specified values):
– targeted‑culling‑percentage (e.g., 50 % of post‑harvest deer in the culling area),
– culling_area (size: None, 1 mile², 5 mile², 9 mile², or 25 mile²; 2.59, 12.95, 23.31, or 64.75 km²) centered on the previous year’s positive test location,
– effort (None, Once, or Repeated),
– added‑dmap‑harvest (percentage increase in antlerless harvest within DMAP area, e.g., 10 %),
– dmap_area (size: None, 9, 25, 49, or 81 mile²; 23.31, 64.75, 126.91, or 209.79 km²) centered on detection locations,
– added‑antlerless‑harvest (percentage change for the entire WMU, e.g., +8 %),
– added‑yearling‑harvest (percentage change for yearling males, e.g., +25 %),
– added‑adult‑harvest (percentage change for adult males, e.g., –5 %).
If "All" is selected, all above response mechanisms are applied except those set to neutral values (e.g., 0 % or None).

Define export variables to be recorded each month: total deer count, proportion infected, detection flag (whether CWD was detected in hunter‑harvested deer), number of 1 mile² cells containing ≥ 1 infected deer, and the maximum distance from the initially infected cell to any infected cell.
Run the simulations using the chosen parallelisation method (future on a PC or clustermq on the HPC).
